key_insight: Jointly training subgrid-scale and wall closures inside a differentiable CFD solver yields better wall-bounded turbulence predictions than fitting either closure alone.
engineering_relevance: This approach improves WMLES robustness across Reynolds numbers, meshes, and domains while reducing the need for case-specific retraining.
method: Hybrid neural-CFD framework with end-to-end backpropagation through the flow solver
Two composed closures: neural network + fixed differentiable layer for SGS and wall modeling
Training uses only low-order statistics, then reuses the learned closures across cases
evidence_signal: Across a posteriori tests at Re_theta = 600-6500, the method outperforms WMLES baselines, extrapolates beyond the training Reynolds number range, and transfers to unseen grids and domains while matching mean velocity and energy spectra.
watch_item: Because the gains depend on differentiable solver integration and joint optimization, implementation complexity and solver/closure coupling may limit straightforward adoption.
paper_title: Differentiable Hybrid Neural-CFD Modelling of Wall-Bounded Turbulence: Coupled Learning of Subgrid-Scale and Wall Closures
